text:
And often to our comfort shall we find
The sharded beetle in a safer hold
Than is the full-wing’d eagle.
plain: The small, quiet creature is often safer than the one flying highest. Height is exposure.

text:
Then was I as a tree
Whose boughs did bend with fruit. But in one night
A storm, or robbery, call it what you will,
Shook down my mellow hangings, nay, my leaves,
And left me bare to weather.
plain: You can be at the top and lose it all in one night. Favor is not something you own.

text:
Yet famine,
Ere clean it o’erthrow nature, makes it valiant.
Plenty and peace breeds cowards; hardness ever
Of hardiness is mother.
plain: Comfort makes you soft. Hardship is what breeds the hard.

text:
The sweat of industry would dry and die
But for the end it works to.
plain: Hard work only feels worth it when you can see what it's for.

text:
Come, our stomachs
Will make what’s homely savoury; weariness
Can snore upon the flint, when resty sloth
Finds the down pillow hard.
plain: Work makes plain food taste great and a rock feel like a bed. Laziness finds even a pillow too hard.

text:
Those that I reverence, those I fear—the wise;
At fools I laugh, not fear them.
plain: Fear the wise. Don't give fools that much power over you.

text:
I know not why
I love this youth, and I have heard you say
Love’s reason’s without reason.
plain: Love doesn't come with a reason. You don't get to argue it into being.

text:
Fear no more the heat o’ th’ sun,
Nor the furious winter’s rages;
Thou thy worldly task hast done,
Home art gone, and ta’en thy wages.
Golden lads and girls all must,
As chimney-sweepers, come to dust.
plain: Everyone ends up as dust, golden or not. So the weather of today can't be that big.
Kings, scholars and doctors all end the same. The powerful have no hold on the dead.

text:
Thersites’ body is as good as Ajax’,
When neither are alive.
plain: The coward and the hero are equal once they're dead. Rank is temporary.

text:
The ground that gave them first has them again.
Their pleasures here are past, so is their pain.
plain: Pleasure and pain both end. The earth takes everyone back.

text:
Be cheerful; wipe thine eyes.
Some falls are means the happier to arise.
plain: Some falls set up the better rise. Wipe your face and keep going.

text:
All other doubts, by time let them be clear’d:
Fortune brings in some boats that are not steer’d.
plain: Time clears most doubts. And luck sometimes lands good things nobody steered.

text:
What pleasure, sir, find we in life, to lock it
From action and adventure?
plain: What's the point of a life you keep locked away from action?

text:
Let me make men know
More valour in me than my habits show.
plain: Don't let your clothes or your status say how much you have in you. Show it.

text:
To shame the guise o’ th’ world, I will begin
The fashion less without and more within.
plain: Care less about the outside and more about what's inside.
People who live off someone else's favor are dreaming. They wake up with nothing.
Real power over an enemy is the power to let them go.

text:
Hath Britain all the sun that shines? Day, night,
Are they not but in Britain? I’ th’ world’s volume
Our Britain seems as of it, but not in’t;
In a great pool a swan’s nest.
plain: Your small corner is not the world. There is more sun and more room out there.

text:
I see before me, man. Nor here, nor here,
Nor what ensues, but have a fog in them
That I cannot look through.
plain: Nobody sees what's coming. Everything ahead is fog, so you move anyway.

text:
No, ’tis slander,
Whose edge is sharper than the sword, whose tongue
Outvenoms all the worms of Nile, whose breath
Rides on the posting winds and doth belie
All corners of the world.
plain: A lie travels faster and cuts deeper than a blade.

text: A little more than kin, and less than kind.
plain: Related to him, but nothing like him in spirit.

text: Seems, madam! Nay, it is; I know not seems.
plain: I'm not performing grief. It's real. I don't do appearances.

text:
How weary, stale, flat, and unprofitable
Seem to me all the uses of this world!
plain: Some days everything looks gray and pointless. Hamlet felt it too, and wrote it down.

text:
He was a man, take him for all in all,
I shall not look upon his like again.
plain: Some people can't be replaced, and you only know it after they're gone.

text:
Be wary then, best safety lies in fear.
Youth to itself rebels, though none else near.
plain: Be careful. The young are their own worst enemy even with nobody around.

text:
And to my mind, though I am native here,
And to the manner born, it is a custom
More honour’d in the breach than the observance.
plain: Some habits are better broken than kept, however old they are.

text:
Why, what should be the fear?
I do not set my life at a pin’s fee;
And for my soul, what can it do to that,
Being a thing immortal as itself?
plain: Once you stop treating your life as precious, fear has nothing left to take.

text:
My fate cries out,
And makes each petty artery in this body
As hardy as the Nemean lion’s nerve.
plain: When you know what you're called to do, your body finds a strength it didn't have.

text: Something is rotten in the state of Denmark.
plain: Something at the top is wrong, and you can feel it before you can prove it.

text:
And duller shouldst thou be than the fat weed
That rots itself in ease on Lethe wharf,
Wouldst thou not stir in this.
plain: Anyone who stays comfortable when it matters is rotting.

text:
My tables. Meet it is I set it down,
That one may smile, and smile, and be a villain!
plain: A friendly face tells you nothing. Plenty of villains smile.

text:
And therefore as a stranger give it welcome.
There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio,
Than are dreamt of in your philosophy.
plain: Reality is bigger than your theory of it. Stay open.

text:
The time is out of joint. O cursed spite,
That ever I was born to set it right.
plain: The world is broken and somehow fixing it landed on you.

text:
My liege and madam, to expostulate
What majesty should be, what duty is,
Why day is day, night night, and time is time
Were nothing but to waste night, day and time.
Therefore, since brevity is the soul of wit,
And tediousness the limbs and outward flourishes,
I will be brief.
plain: Say it short. Long-windedness is just padding on a thin idea.

text: Ay sir, to be honest, as this world goes, is to be one man picked out of ten thousand.
plain: An honest person is rare. Be the one in ten thousand.

text:
Happy in that we are not over-happy;
On Fortune’s cap we are not the very button.
plain: Not at the very top and not at the bottom. That middle is a fine place to be.

text: Why, then ’tis none to you; for there is nothing either good or bad but thinking makes it so.
plain: Things aren't good or bad until your mind says so. Change the thought, change the weight.

text: O God, I could be bounded in a nutshell, and count myself a king of infinite space, were it not that I have bad dreams.
plain: A tiny life would be enough if your own mind would leave you alone.

text: What a piece of work is man, how noble in reason, how infinite in faculties, in form and moving, how express and admirable; in action how like an angel, in apprehension, how like a god: the beauty of the world, the paragon of animals. And yet, to me, what is this quintessence of dust?
plain: People are astonishing, and also just dust. Both are true and it can get you down.

text: Use every man after his desert, and who should ’scape whipping?
plain: If everyone got what they deserved, nobody would get off. Be generous.

text:
Yet I,
A dull and muddy-mettled rascal, peak
Like John-a-dreams, unpregnant of my cause,
And can say nothing.
plain: Watching someone else burn for nothing, while you drift with a real cause and do nothing.

text:
For murder, though it have no tongue, will speak
With most miraculous organ.
plain: Hidden wrongs come out eventually, one way or another.

text:
The play’s the thing
Wherein I’ll catch the conscience of the King.
plain: Stage the truth and see who flinches.

text:
’Tis too much prov’d, that with devotion’s visage
And pious action we do sugar o’er
The devil himself.
plain: A holy face and good deeds can cover up something rotten. We all do it.

text:
Thus conscience does make cowards of us all,
And thus the native hue of resolution
Is sicklied o’er with the pale cast of thought,
And enterprises of great pith and moment,
With this regard their currents turn awry
And lose the name of action.
plain: Overthinking kills big plans. The more you worry at a decision, the less you do it.

text: I am very proud, revengeful, ambitious, with more offences at my beck than I have thoughts to put them in, imagination to give them shape, or time to act them in. What should such fellows as I do crawling between earth and heaven?
plain: Hamlet's honest about his flaws. Naming your worst traits is where self-mastery starts.

text: Be thou as chaste as ice, as pure as snow, thou shalt not escape calumny.
plain: Be spotless and people will still talk. Live right and stop managing gossip.

text:
O, what a noble mind is here o’erthrown!
The courtier’s, soldier’s, scholar’s, eye, tongue, sword,
Th’expectancy and rose of the fair state,
The glass of fashion and the mould of form,
Th’observ’d of all observers, quite, quite down!
plain: Even the most promising mind can fall. Guard yours.
